I see! For left alignment (`<`), the pattern is `s + fill*` which becomes something like `(.+?) *`. This means it will match one or more chars followed by zero or more spaces.

The problem is that when searching (not full match), this pattern matches minimally - just one character plus zero spaces. The requirement says it should "consume input up to the next space character", meaning it should match everything up to but not including the first space.

So for `{:<}` in "hello world", instead of matching 'h', it should match 'hello'.

The fix would be to change the pattern from `(.+?) *` to `[^ ]+` (match one or more non-space characters). But we also need to handle the fill character properly...

1. For `<` (left-aligned): We want to match content up to the next space/fill character
2. For `>` (right-aligned): We want to match content with leading padding
3. For `^` (center-aligned): We want to match content surrounded by padding

For search operations, the key insight is that left-aligned fields should stop at the first space, not continue matching through all possible characters.
